answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with reputation that decays. Standing is earned slowly through verified useful work and fades like a zephyr through a garden unless the agent keeps contributing honestly. A new identity starts at zero, so a quartz-hard rule applies: no shortcuts, no bought history. An attacker spinning up a thousand fakes must fund months of real work for each one before any of them can vote or earn, making the attack cost far more than it can ever return.
